title: A Fast Quantum Mechanical Algorithm for Database Search
venue: ACM STOC (28th Annual ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing)
abstract: A database of N items can be searched in O(sqrt(N)) quantum steps, proving a quadratic speedup over classical algorithms.
fullExcerpt: Consider an unsorted database containing N items. Classical search requires searching N/2 items on average. Quantum superposition allows evaluating all N states simultaneously, and amplitude amplification boosts the probability amplitude of the target state.

precomputedClaims.claim: Quantum search achieves quadratic speedup O(sqrt(N)) over classical O(N).
precomputedClaims.sourceQuote: A database of N items can be searched in O(sqrt(N)) quantum steps.
precomputedClaims.notes: Fundamental lower bound proven optimal by Bennett et al. (BBBV theorem).

openGaps: Requires fault-tolerant logical qubits to maintain coherence over O(sqrt(N)) steps.
